Hi Connor,

We signed up for Redwood last week and would love a short demo to understand fit for our product search use case. Quick context: we run semantic search and reranking over ~120M SKUs; typical queries are short (10–40 tokens) but we expect spikes during campaigns.

High-level asks:
- Walkthrough of inference options (hosted vs dedicated) for this scale
- Guidance on latency & batching tradeoffs for search traffic
- Rough cost ballpark for a 6–8 week pilot (50k reqs/day average; spikes to ~200k/day)

Ideal pilot timeline: kickoff in 4–6 weeks. Could you propose a few demo slots next week? I cc'd Tom (engineering) who will join.

Thanks,
Emma Li
Head of Search, CrateAI
emma@crateai.com

Hi Emma — welcome and thanks for the context. Happy to run through a tailored demo. Before we lock a slot, a few quick qualification questions so we can focus the session and pull the right materials:

1) Peak concurrency / QPS during spikes (rough number)?
2) Average tokens per query and whether you need embeddings for retrieval or just generation/rerank?
3) Any PII / regulated data in the queries? (affects Private options)
4) Cloud/region preference and whether you need a VPC/on‑prem proof of concept
5) Who will own the pilot internally (engineering lead + PM)?

Proposed 3 slots (all PT):
- Tue Mar 9, 10:00–10:30am
- Wed Mar 10, 2:00–2:30pm
- Thu Mar 11, 9:00–9:30am

I also attached our short SDR intake form (SDR-intake-form.pdf) — if you can fill that out it helps speed the cost estimate.

If any of those times don't work, tell me preferences and we can adjust.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise SDR, Redwood Inference

Thanks Connor — answers below inline. I filled the intake form and attached it.

1) Peak concurrency: around 300–400 concurrent requests during big campaigns; baseline concurrency usually 8–12.
2) Average tokens: ~30 tokens/query. We use embeddings for retrieval + a small reranker model.
3) PII: minimal — product names and anonymized account ids; we treat user identifiers lightly but would prefer isolation for the pilot if it's not onerous.
4) Region: prefer us-east (we run infra in AWS us-east-1). No on‑prem required at this stage.
5) Pilot owners: Tom Harris (cc'd) will be the engineering lead; I am the PM.

Pilot target: we'd like to launch a short proof-of-concept in ~4 weeks if feasible.

From the slots you suggested, Wed Mar 10 2pm PT works best. Can you send calendar invite and brief agenda (30m)? Also any preliminary cost ballpark would be helpful so we can prepare stakeholders.

Cheers,
Emma

Attachment: SDR-intake-form.pdf (completed)

From: ben_carter@redwood.example.com

Hi Emma — Ben on solutions engineering. Quick notes based on your answers:

- Concurrency: with 300–400 peak concurrent requests we typically recommend Dedicated for predictable latency and cost during spikes; Hosted can work for early POC if you accept variable latencies.
- Throughput: with ~30 tokens/query and embeddings + reranker you should budget for both embedding units and token generation; I can run a back-of-envelope tonight if you share a 24h traffic sample or expected peak QPS number.
- Isolation: pilot in a VPC/Dedicated node can be arranged; it's usually a small setup overhead.

Agenda suggestion for Wed 10 (30m):
- 5m: intros + goals
- 10m: architecture options (hosted/dedicated/private) + latency/cost tradeoffs
- 10m: pilot checklist & next steps (MVP scope, data ingestion, SSO, MLPs)
- 5m: Q&A and next actions (MVP kickoff, SOW/estimate)

I can also share a quick cost estimate if Tom can paste a simple traffic profile (avg reqs/hr and peak reqs/hr).

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.example.com
